narrative.overview: The interface is a quiet instrument panel. The 3D universe is the show; the 2D layer is dark glass and small, precise readouts floating in front of it. Text never competes with the scene: it sits on translucent panels or on a soft dark scrim, and the camera's warp between stops does the dramatic work.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas, light text, always color-scheme: dark.
Three signal accents (violet, amber, mint), each with one job.
Flat translucent glass over the live scene; no drop shadows.
Readability over bright 3D is solved with scrims and text-shadow, not by dimming the scene.
Motion is short fades and small translates; prefers-reduced-motion collapses it.

rules.name: The Signal Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet, amber and mint are labels and focus rings, not surfaces. If an accent fills a large area, it is wrong.

rules.name: The White CTA Rule
rules.body: The single primary action on a stop is solid white with black text, the only fully opaque light element in the system.

rules.name: The Fluid Display Rule
rules.body: Only the hero name scales fluidly; everything else steps at the sm breakpoint so 320px stays legible.

rules.name: The Flat Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay flat at rest. Hover may translate or scale; it never adds a shadow.

dos: Do keep text on glass panels or a dark scrim whenever it overlays the canvas.
Do use mint for labels, amber for the role eyebrow, violet for focus.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px and layouts clean at 320px.
Do keep motion to short fades and small translates, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add shadows, neon glows or gradient fills to panels.
Don't fill large areas with an accent colour.
Don't put body text directly on the canvas without a scrim.
Don't introduce a third typeface or a third level of panel treatment.
